- One <style> block, centered dark-themed layout (system font, page background #0f172a or similar dark slate), HUD bar above canvas showing mode name and two colored score chips, <canvas> 600x600, absolutely-positioned overlay <div>s over the canvas for the start menu and game over screen (semi-transparent dark background with backdrop blur), one <script> block at the end. Small explanatory comments, clean organization.

GAME CORE (JS):
- Grid: 30x30 cells, CELL = 20px, canvas 600x600. Walls kill (no wrap-around).
- Constants: GRID=30, base tick 100ms, tick speeds up by 2ms per food eaten, minimum 60ms.
- Two snakes: SNAKE1 green (#4ade80) starts left side heading right; SNAKE2 orange (#fb923c) starts right side heading left. Each snake is an array of {x,y} cells, head at index 0, plus current direction, queued direction, score, alive flag, and controller ('human' or 'cpu').
- Single shared food: red (#ef4444) circle on a random free cell not occupied by either snake.
- Game loop with requestAnimationFrame + time accumulator; each tick: apply queued directions (a queued direction is ignored if it is a 180-degree reversal of the current direction), CPU snakes compute their direction via AI before moving, then compute all new heads simultaneously, then resolve collisions in this order: (1) head outside grid -> that snake dies; (2) head hits any snake body segment; tail cells that will vacate this tick (non-growing snakes' last segment) do NOT count as collision; (3) head-to-head same cell or head swaps cell with other head -> both die. Any death immediately ends the game.
- Eating: when a head lands on the food cell, that snake's score +1, it grows this tick (tail not removed), food respawns on a random free cell, tick interval decreases.
- Score +1 per food. Snake length starts at 4.

CPU AI (function chooseCpuDirection(snake, food, otherSnake)):
- Candidate directions: all 4 except the reverse of current direction.
- Discard candidates that immediately hit a wall or any occupied cell (bodies of both snakes, ignoring vacating tails as above).
- For each surviving candidate run a flood fill (BFS over free cells from the candidate head cell) counting reachable free area; a candidate is "safe" if reachable area >= snake length (or >= all remaining free cells).
- Among safe candidates prefer the one minimizing Manhattan distance to food; tie-break: keep current direction, else any. Head-on avoidance: if the other snake's head can enter the candidate cell next tick, strongly deprioritize it.
- If no candidate passes the flood-fill safety test, pick the immediate-safe one with the largest reachable area; if none are immediate-safe, keep current direction (dies).

MODES & CONTROLS:
- States: MENU, PLAYING, GAMEOVER.
- Start menu overlay: big title "SNAKE", subtitle, and three options with keyboard selection: press 1 = "HUMAN vs HUMAN", 2 = "CPU vs HUMAN", 3 = "CPU vs CPU"; also up/down arrow keys move a highlighted selection and Enter/Space starts it. Show control legend: "P1: WASD (green) — P2: Arrow keys (orange)".
- Mode HUMAN vs HUMAN: SNAKE1 controlled by WASD, SNAKE2 by arrow keys.
- Mode CPU vs HUMAN: SNAKE1 is CPU, SNAKE2 is human and may use BOTH arrow keys and WASD.
- Mode CPU vs CPU: both snakes are CPU.
- Keyboard listener on window: preventDefault for arrows/space/WASD to stop page scrolling; routes keys by state (menu selection, in-game turns, game-over restart).
- HUD: mode name, "P1" score chip in green, "P2" score chip in orange, both updating live during play.
- Game over overlay: winner text ("P1 WINS!", "P2 WINS!", or "DRAW") with both final scores and reason hints; buttons-in-text: "R or Enter — play again (same mode)" and "M or Esc — main menu". Restarting resets scores, snakes, food, speed. In GAMEOVER, pressing R or Enter/Space restarts the same mode; M or Esc returns to menu.
- Draw function: dark board, subtle grid lines, food as glowing red circle, snakes as rounded rectangles with slightly brighter head and small eyes on the head; dead state not needed to render since overlay appears.

POLISH:
- All text in English. No external fonts/libraries. Code in a single IIFE or plain top-level script with const/let."}
